Families across Kentucky have suffered from the opioid and substance abuse epidemic for far too long. After years of heartbreaking loss, there is finally a glimmer of hope: overdose deaths in Kentucky declined by nearly 23% last year. This progress is encouraging, but our work is far from over. We must keep dangerous drugs out of our communities and support those in recovery. As long as I serve in the Senate, I will keep fighting to prevent and treat addiction in Kentucky.
https://t.co/RHMf9oUJJ

posts.text: On Memorial Day, we remember those who put their lives on the line in defense of American freedom. My father was a foot soldier who fought during World War II on the Eastern front. His bravery, and the bravery and determination of his fellow soldiers helped us achieve victory over evil, and so many of his brothers in arms did not make it home. So today we honor them and pledge to move forward with pride and the continued strength to come together to protect and defend our country.

posts.text: This week, I’m honored to join communities throughout the U.S. in celebrating National Police Week. Every day, law enforcement officers across the country answer the call to serve and defend our communities. I’m proud to continue my work in the Senate supporting these devoted public servants—federal, state, and local—who put their lives on the line for the security of the American people, and I’m grateful for their bravery and tireless efforts to protect Kentuckians across the Commonwealth.
